note: Fresh tracks (23 Nov 2026, hunting thread; Dave: 'extrapolate from them and see what would make for a fun hunting game'): each footfall of a live animal drawn within draw_m of the player (animal_view stepped, read only) leaves a print that fades over life_s real seconds, life_mult times longer at Tracking 100, so a hunter can follow the animal itself. A print only once the kind has moved min_gap_m from its last one; at most max_prints at once (one walking deer at 1.3 m/s lays about two a second, so 480 hold a few minutes of a few animals; a herd fills it sooner and the oldest go first). Shapes by kind; birds and frogs leave none. Client only. Provisional.
read_note: Reading a fresh print: look right at it (read_aim_cos, about 10 degrees) within read_m and press E. Whose it is and how old for anyone; a predator's adds a warning (Dave's core rule: the game does not want you to die unless you do something deliberately stupid, so warn plainly); from read_way_level (Dave's 10 for trails on the map) which way it was heading.

read.warning: A hunter is about: keep your eyes open.
